name: Peavey 5150 Block Letter (134000)
description: Peavey EVH 5150 'Block Letter', catalogue unit 134000, from the 1992 Peavey drawing set (CB #98002910, CODE 8150510): input stage V1A, the K4A rhythm/lead input pads, the CLEAN PRE and LEAD PRE gain pots, V1B / V2A cold clipper / V2B / V5B / V5A, the K4A-K4B-K1A-K1B relay channel switching, the three-band tone stack with the K1B mid shift, the CLEAN/ULTRA POST gain, the effects loop cathode follower V3B and recovery V3A, the V4 long-tail-pair inverter, four 6L6GC with the SR2873 plate clamps, the 1.7 k output transformer into an 8 ohm cab,, and the negative feedback from the 8 ohm tap through R56 39K and the series RESONANCE element (C12 || VR8) into the PRESENCE shunt (C8 || C62 + VR9) and C30 into the bottom of the inverter tail (R51 10K / R57 4.7K), with C31 tying the V4A grid to that node. R85 220K and R81 2.2M on sheet 1 are not feedback parts. The effects path is the 1992 drawing's (Addendum 9 in work/circuit-netlists/wave-e/peavey-5150-block-letter.notes.md): HIGH wiper -> VR6 CLEAN POST / VR7 ULTRA POST, K2B picks the wiper -> the CLAMP node (R81 2.2M; Q7 J174 mute JFET with its gate at +22 V through R84 1M / C55 .1; CR21/CR22 1N4148 to the 24 V rails) -> C52 .022 -> V3B cathode follower (R79 bootstrapped) -> C53 .33 / R103 100K / C65 .33 / R33 100K -> K3B/K3A at rest (the unpatched loop: the RETURN jack's tip switch makes the energized state the same circuit) -> R85 220K -> C11 .047 -> V3A grid with R26 1M. The CLAMP mute trigger (TRIG, R83, C54, MAC97) is open at idle and is not modelled. The relay coils and the 24 V coil rail are not in the audio path and are modelled as the switches they drive.

sources.title: Peavey EVH 120 PREAMP BD schematic set, CB #98002910, code 8150510, date 5-FEB-92, sheets 1-3 of 3 (sheet 1 preamp board, sheet 2 inverter + bias + HT supply, sheet 3 power amp board)
sources.note: AUTHORITATIVE for unit 134000. 1-bit 300 dpi scans, portrait scans of landscape drawings: page 1 is 2328x3105, page 2 2352x3189, page 3 2472x3525; every page was rotated 90 deg before reading. Values were read at 1:1 and at 2.2x-10x on crops, never from a downscale.

sources.title: Peavey EVH 5150 schematic, page 5 of 5 (the complete folded sheet, 4760x3122)
sources.note: A LATER Peavey revision with different designators and a different tone stack (C12 .0033 / C8 .01 / C62 .033 / VR9 10K PRES against the 1992 board's C11/C59/C18/C21). Used ONLY as a geometric cross-check at 8x where the 1992 sheet's junction dots merge: the preamp stages, the K4A/K4B/K1A contact geometry and the power amp agree between the two.

sources.title: EVH 5150 redraw, `VH 5150 COMBO`, Peavey drawing 99505263 REV A (4290x3060, via blueguitar.org / Wayback 2006-05-15, file evh_5150.gif)
sources.note: A THIRD revision. Used only where the 1992 board's tone-stack junction dots merge (the addendum-4 read: three series branches between two vertical rails, slope R, the K1B mid shift) and for the presence/resonance block (R108 39K / C61 .0033 || VR8 1M || C63 .033 || C64 .01 / VR10 10K), whose values agree with the 1992 board's block.

multirate.note: Event-local oversampling (docs §10.48, §10.62): base 192 kHz, 8 substeps (1.536 MHz) on every LTE event. With 4 substeps (768 kHz) the knees' integration error folds about 768 kHz at -55.5 dB (aliasing gate, own-mains mask, 0.5 FS; harmonic 270 at 15 kHz); with 8: -66.3 / -68.2 / -67.6 dB at 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 FS. Band-limited ngspice truth (p5150v2bl), audio band, lead / rock DI: spk 0.308 / 0.667 -> 0.274 / 0.602 %, p4a 0.220 / 0.491 -> 0.107 / 0.262 %

newton.note: Event substeps (docs §10.64): the tube ports of every LTE substep converge at 10x the full step's tube tolerance (1e-2); every other port and the full step keep theirs (all ports at 10x fail the clamp network's SPICE gate). T/8 substep Newton 1.84 -> 1.60 iterations; 9900X real / driven -2.6 / -2.9 %, block p99 -4.4 % (M4 Pro instructions mean / p99 -3.1 / -5.3 %). Band-limited ngspice truth unchanged to the 4th digit (audio, lead / rock DI: spk 0.274 / 0.602 %, p4a 0.107 / 0.262 %); aliasing within 0.5 dB of 1x on both tones (2900 Hz -66.8 / -68.1 / -67.3, 3130 Hz -65.3 / -65.2 / -55.8 dB). CE_SUBTOL=1 restores 1x.

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS = 1.5 x the 73.2 V peak measured at the speaker with the Lead channel dimed (channel=Lead, lead=1, post=1, 220 Hz, 30 mV in, 176.4 kHz, 4 s, last 2 s; 34.0 V RMS; every knob at 1 gives 73.4 V pk). Re-measured 2026-11-15 after the loop path was re-traced to the 1992 drawing and the CLAMP network's static parts added (notes Addendum 9); was 104 (69.5 V pk).

SR2873.note: SR2873 = 1N5406-class 3 A 600 V fast-recovery rectifier used here as a plate clamp. No published SPICE card; the 1N400x-class card the library already uses for 1N4001 is fitted, which is what matters for a clamp that only conducts on flyback.

J174.note: J174 P-channel (onsemi J174-J177 datasheet: VGS(off) +5 ... +10 V, IDSS 20-135 mA, rDS(on) <= 85 ohm): SPICE vto -7 (centre), beta 1 mA/V^2 -> IDSS 49 mA, rDS(on) 1/(2 beta |vto|) = 71 ohm; Cgs = Cgd = 5.5 pF, the Calogic J174 sheet's Csg(off) / Cdg(off) at VGS 10 V. Same convention as the J175 card in ssl-4000g-bus-comp-130000.

parts.label: K2A: gates the Lead pre wiper into the V1B mixer node (closed in Lead)
parts.note: INFERRED, and the one contact in this netlist that is not read off a drawing. The board carries four audio relay poles besides K4A/K4B/K1A/K1B (K2A, K2B, K3A, K3B); they sit in the coil-drive block on sheet 1 that the notes list as unresolved. Leaving the lead wiper permanently on the mixer was measured and is wrong: both gain knobs then fight over one node (with the Lead knob at 0.5 the Rhythm knob moved the output only 15.0 -> 16.5 V, i.e. it did not work). Gating the lead wiper with K2A on the Channel control is the minimum change that makes the two catalogue gain controls independent, and it is what the relay count and the amp's documented channel behaviour require. Flagged in the notes.

parts.note: p2@300 2050,900,3000,1350. TRIG, R83 47, C54 .1 and the triac are open at idle and are not modelled; the static parts are, because the post wiper reaches them (notes Addendum 9 §3).

The opposite phasing turns the loop positive and the amp bursts at low frequency.
parts.note: unverified: no source gives Raa or DCR for T2 70500207. 1.7 k p-p is the value the other Peavey 6L6 120 W netlists use; 8 ohm tap turns = 2*sqrt(8/1700), 4 ohm tap = 2*sqrt(4/1700). DCR 20 ohm per half, leakage 3 mH per half, lm 80 H and lsat 5 V s are typical 100 W-class values. Feedback is taken from the 8 ohm tap (the speaker node): sheet 2 wires J99 8 ohm to the FEEDBACK net in every S3 position (5150_evh.pdf p2@300 2138,130,3038,620) and sheet 3 takes FEDBACK off the W (8 OHM) lead (5150_evh.pdf p3@300 2625,560,3325,1000). The 4 ohm tap winding the netlist used to carry for the feedback is removed: with the cab on the 8 ohm tap nothing loads it. parts.label: C62 .033 uF presence capacitor in parallel with C8
VR9 PRESENCE 10K-A rheostat to ground
parts.note: Wiper (pin 3) strapped to pin 1 (the C8/C62 node), pin 2 to the chassis-ground node, CW arrow toward pin 2 (5150_evh.pdf p1@300 2725,1120,2955,1310): a two-terminal rheostat in series with C8 || C62 = 133 nF to ground, 10K at CCW and 0 at CW, so CW = more presence. 10KAVB = 10K audio taper; the log end is pin 1 (CCW), so the series resistance stays above ~6.7K to 0.75 of travel and the shelf comes in over the top quarter of rotation. This is the drawn part and wiring, not a modelling choice. parts.label: VR8 RESONANCE 1M-A rheostat across C12, in series in the feedback path
parts.note: Pin 1 on J34 (with C12), pin 2 on J35, wiper (pin 3) strapped to pin 2, and the CW arrow points at pin 2 (5150_evh.pdf p1@300 2545,1040,2765,1270). So the resistance across C12 is the pin1-wiper track, 0 at CCW and 1M at CW: turning it up opens the low-frequency feedback path through C12 (6.8 nF) and raises the low end, the bass shelf the 5150 manual describes. Peavey pin 1 = CCW, pin 2 = CW is the sheet-wide convention (VR7 ULTRA POST: pin 1 grounded, pin 2 = the hot end).
